topSignals.title: Bloom Energy joins the S&P 500 at tomorrow's open (Sept 21) — the first pure-play energy company added to the index since 2022, with its SOFC-for-AI-datacenters growth story cited as the explicit rationale.
topSignals.text: BE, Illumina and Everpure replace Molson Coors, Trade Desk and Builders FirstSource in the quarterly rebalance (announced Sept 4). Stock closed Sept 19 around $265.63, a modest pullback from the $270-288 range seen Sept 17-18, still up ~200%+ YTD; index-fund buying tied to inclusion is now the incremental flow driver rather than new commercial news. No new contracts or technical disclosures in the last 24-48h. Yahoo Finance | S&P Global

topSignals.title: Both Senate vehicles for shifting data-center grid costs onto operators are now confirmed dead — not just stalled.
topSignals.text: Fuller picture of the Sept 17 standoff (previously logged as "Heinrich objects to House bill"): Sen. Heinrich (D-NM) blocked the House's 417-3 Ratepayer Protection Act via unanimous consent, calling it toothless; he then sought unanimous consent for his own alternative, the GRID Savings Act (FERC-enforced, 150 MW threshold, bans cost-rollup into residential rates) — and Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-OH) objected, killing that one too. Net effect for Dominic: the "data centers will be forced to pay their own grid costs" narrative that had been lifting fuel-cell stocks (FCEL +13%, BE +3% on the House vote) has lost its near-term legislative vehicle; Trump-Thune talks (logged Sept 19) remain the only live thread, and the Senate has only weeks left before the Nov 3 midterm recess. The Hill | mGrid

topSignals.title: Priority stacks Elcogen and Topsoe: fourth consecutive quiet day — no new announcements from either.
topSignals.text: Elcogen unchanged since the Sept 15 Shanghai HyEnergy supply agreement (elcoStack E3000 G2, ELCO I Tallinn 360 MW/yr). Topsoe unchanged since the Sept 7 Uniper e-methanol FEED contract; SOEC-only Herning factory (500 MW/yr) remains the flagship asset, SOFC/data-center pathway still deferred under the May 2026 roadmap review. Direct site checks (elcogen.com, topsoe.com/press-releases) confirm no new releases in the last 24-48h.

items.text: Elcogen (priority): No new news. Standing status unchanged — see Top Signal #3.
Topsoe (priority): No new news. Standing status unchanged — see Top Signal #3.
Ceres Power: No new stack/cell news; H1 2026 results still due before market open Wednesday Sept 23 (consensus loss ~$0.0644/share, revenue ~$34.75M) — unchanged.
No new stack/cell announcements found from Bloom Energy, FuelCell Energy, Sunfire, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, or Aisin in the last 24-48h.

Top story — see Top Signal #2:* both the House-passed Ratepayer Protection Act and Sen. Heinrich's GRID Savings Act alternative are now dead in the Senate after the Sept 17 dual-objection standoff (Heinrich blocks the House bill; Moreno blocks Heinrich's). Standing background unchanged: Trump-Thune conversations on a companion bill (Sept 18, no text yet), Sen. Van Hollen's "Power for the People Act" (S.3682) and Sen. Wyden's data-center excise-tax white paper remain pending as separate vehicles; PJM backstop reliability auction (bid window Sept 30-Oct 21); FERC co-location transmission-service order in compliance-filing phase; FERC RM26-4 Section 206 show-cause orders (responses due Nov 16); Virginia's $0.011/kWh self-generation tax; US ITC 48E 30% fuel-cell credit (natural-gas/biogas SOFC qualifies post-OBBBA); New York's permit moratorium; Texas's development pause; Germany's EnEfG-Novelle (pending) and EEG-Novelle 2027 (first Bundestag reading Sept 24).

Bloom Energy (BE): Closed ~$265.63 Sept 19, pulling back modestly from the $270-288 range of Sept 17-18 ahead of tomorrow's S&P 500 entry (Top Signal #1). Securities class-action (covering purchasers Feb 27 2025-Jul 8 2026, scandium-sourcing allegations) lead-plaintiff deadline Sept 28; Q3 earnings Oct 27.

FuelCell Energy (FCEL): Closed $18.12 Sept 19 (range $17.17-18.38). New since last digest: Citi initiated coverage with a Neutral rating and $19 price target; Craig-Hallum initiated with a Buy rating and $22 price target — both following the Sept 2 Q3 print (data-center capacity agreement, 16.9% single-day drop on the wider loss). Director John Livingston bought 26.3K shares (~$247K) on Sept 14. Robbins LLP lead-plaintiff-deadline reminder for the June 4-Sept 1 class period remains outstanding (deadline already passed Sept 18).
Ceres Power (CWR.L): H1 2026 results due Sept 23 before market open — unchanged.

Patent-landscape read (PatSnap, background, not dated to this window): SOFC/SOEC filings increasingly converge on reversible cell designs (fuel-cell-under-load / electrolyzer-under-surplus-power); despite foundational filings from University of Florida Research Foundation and Honeywell, no dominant approach has emerged for sub-700°C SOFC with long-term durability — flagged as a "white space" in cathode three-phase-boundary engineering and bismuth-oxide electrolyte stabilization. Directional context only, not a new filing event.
Otherwise quiet — no new SOFC-specific patent or national-lab item independently dated to the last 24-48h.

lcoe.text: New MCFC (not SOFC) system LCOE study, for cross-reference: International Journal of Energy Research (Wiley, 2026) "Cross-System Comparative Techno-Economic and Environmental Evaluation of MCFC Integration in Power and Biogas Upgrading Systems" reports LCOE of $0.052-0.056/kWh for molten-carbonate systems, highly sensitive to CO2-utilization pathway and stack price, with SOFC-microturbine hybrids noted to outperform MCFC-microturbine designs on efficiency and stack cost — a useful comparator data point for the model's SOFC-vs-MCFC competitiveness section, not a direct SOFC input. Wiley

Henry Hub carry-forward, unchanged: futures through September 2026 remain below $3.00/MMBtu; EIA expects spot to stay sub-$3.00 until November; full-year 2026 EIA average estimate ~$3.43-3.44/MMBtu — still below the model's carried $4.00-4.30/MMBtu assumption; worth reconciling.

Regulatory carry-forward, unchanged: both federal cost-shift bills now dead (Top Signal #2) removes near-term downside/upside uncertainty on the "SOFC avoids grid-upgrade cost-shift" argument — a qualitative rather than quantitative LCOE factor, but relevant to risk-adjusting the behind-the-meter case. US ITC 48E 30% credit for natural-gas/biogas SOFC (construction start post-Dec 31 2025, domestic-content thresholds 45%/50%/55% in 2026-28); Virginia's $0.011/kWh self-generation tax; PJM's $555/MW-day backstop ceiling.

Pending calendar: Ceres H1 results (Sept 23), Germany EEG-Novelle first Bundestag reading (Sept 24), Bloom formal S&P 500 entry (Sept 21 open), Bloom lead-plaintiff deadline (Sept 28), PJM backstop bid window (Sept 30-Oct 21), Bloom Q3 earnings (Oct 27).
